raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Adds \`KimiVLForConditionalGeneration\` to \`get_model_params\` in \`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py\`.

Kimi-VL wraps a DeepseekV3-family text backbone inside a vision-language outer config. The MoE fields (\`n_routed_experts\`, \`num_experts_per_tok\`, \`moe_intermediate_size\`, \`hidden_size\`) live on \`config.get_text_config()\`, so the existing default fallback — which reads \`num_local_experts\` off the text_config, Mixtral-style — raises \`AttributeError\` on this architecture.

Same pattern as the \`Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration\` dispatch branch immediately above, and parallel to #40181 which does the same for Gemma4.

After this PR, \`benchmark_moe.py --model moonshotai/Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct --tune\` works without a \`--model-prefix\` hack.

## Test plan
- [x] Confirmed Kimi-VL-A3B-Instruct text_config is a \`DeepseekV3Config\` with the expected fields (\`n_routed_experts=64\`, \`num_experts_per_tok=6\`, \`moe_intermediate_size=1408\`, \`hidden_size=2048\`)
- [x] Tuning sweep driven by these shape values produced the JSON shipped in #40542

## Related
- #40542 — A100 tuning config that this script would generate
- #40181 — same fix pattern for Gemma4

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces support for the KimiVLForConditionalGeneration architecture in the MoE benchmark kernel by extracting model parameters from the inner text configuration. A review comment recommends using recursion to call get_model_params on the text configuration, which would eliminate code duplication and leverage existing logic for the DeepSeek-V3 backbone.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Instead of duplicating the parameter extraction logic for the DeepSeek-V3 backbone, you can use recursion to leverage the existing implementation for text models. This follows the cleaner pattern used for `PixtralForConditionalGeneration` (line 816) and improves maintainability by avoiding hardcoded field names that are already handled in the `DeepseekV2/V3` branch (lines 765-778).

```suggestion
    elif architecture == "KimiVLForConditionalGeneration":
        # Kimi-VL wraps a DeepseekV3-family text backbone; recurse to get
        # its parameters from the inner text_config.
        return get_model_params(config.get_text_config())
```

nodes.body:
Appreciate the suggestion, but recursion doesn't work for Kimi-VL.

`config.get_text_config()` returns a `DeepseekV3Config` with `architectures=None`, so inside `get_model_params` the dispatch key becomes `type(text_config).__name__ == "DeepseekV3Config"` — not `"DeepseekV3ForCausalLM"`. Neither matches any branch, execution falls through to the Mixtral/Llama4 fallback, and that raises `AttributeError: 'DeepseekV3Config' object has no attribute 'num_local_experts'`. Verified locally with `transformers==5.5.4`.

This is presumably why the adjacent `Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration` branch does the same hardcoded-fields pattern rather than recursing (Pixtral can recurse because its sub-backbones are full LLMs whose `config.json` sets `architectures`). Keeping the hardcoded approach here for consistency with the Qwen3VL precedent.
